items.title: v1 list with pageIndex=-1 returns 400 naming PageIndex
items.reason: Reproduces step 1 of the bug exactly: a negative page index reached `Skip(pageSize * pageIndex)` and Postgres failed, surfacing as an empty `500`. Functional layer because only the in-process API against the real database proves the 500 is gone and the problem response is produced by the endpoint pipeline.

items.title: v1 list with pageSize=-1 returns 400 naming PageSize
items.reason: Reproduces step 2: a negative page size reached `Take(pageSize)` and failed with an empty `500`. Separate from case 01 because the problem must name the specific parameter that is wrong; functional layer for the same reason as case 01.

items.title: v2 list with pageIndex=-1 returns 400 naming PageIndex
items.reason: Step 3 repeats the bug on `api-version=2.0`, which maps `/items` to a different endpoint (`ListItems-V2`, with name/type/brand filters); a fix applied only to v1 would leave v2 returning `500`. Functional layer for the same reason as case 01.

items.title: v2 list with pageSize=-1 returns 400 naming PageSize
items.reason: Fourth request of the reproduction: negative page size on `api-version=2.0`. Covers the v2 endpoint for the second parameter so neither rule can be missing on v2. Functional layer for the same reason as case 01.

items.title: v1 list with pageIndex=-1 and pageSize=-1 names both parameters
covers: Expected: the validation problem names the parameter (both invalid)
items.reason: The Expected result says the problem names the invalid parameter; when both are invalid, a check that stops at the first failure would hide the second. Separate case because it checks error aggregation, not either single rule. Functional layer for the same reason as case 01.

items.title: v1 list with pageIndex=0 and pageSize=1 still returns the first page
covers: Expected: page index 0 and page size 1 behave as today
items.reason: The fix must not over-reject: 0 is the smallest valid page index and 1 the smallest valid page size, the values just inside the limits. An off-by-one (`<= 0` on the index, `< 2` on the size) would turn this into a `400`. Functional layer because the response must come from the real query.

items.title: v2 list with pageIndex=0 and pageSize=1 still returns the first page
covers: Expected: page index 0 and page size 1 behave as today
items.reason: Same lower-boundary check as case 06 on the v2 endpoint, which has its own route registration and could be given a different (wrong) rule. Functional layer because the response must come from the real query.

items.title: v1 list with pageIndex=10 and pageSize=10 returns the last partial page
covers: Expected: requests with a page index of 0 or more and a page size of 1 or more behave as today
items.reason: Checks that ordinary paging past the first page is unchanged: with 101 items and page size 10, index 10 is the last page holding one item. Guards against a validation rule that caps or rewrites positive values. Functional layer because skip/take runs in the real database.
